title: Domains collectively
notice: This map records public paraphrases and Lean source locations. It does not reproduce the textbook text.

items.title: Section-retraction pairs
items.summary: Monotone and continuous section-retraction pairs, with a retract equation.

items.title: Properties inherited by monotone retracts
items.summary: Suprema, infima, dcpo structure, pointedness, semilattice/lattice structure, and completeness descend along monotone section-retraction pairs.

items.title: Retraction image of a basis
items.summary: A continuous section-retraction pair sends a basis of the larger dcpo to a basis of the retract.

items.title: Continuous retracts of continuous domains
items.summary: A continuous retract of a continuous domain is continuous.

items.title: Continuous domains as retracts of algebraic domains
items.summary: Every continuous or omega-continuous domain is represented as a continuous retract of an algebraic or omega-algebraic ideal completion.

items.title: Basis ideal completion section-retraction
items.summary: The maps from a domain to the ideal completion of a basis and back form the continuous section-retraction pair used in Theorem 3.1.5.

items.title: Images and directed suprema of continuous idempotents
items.summary: The image of a continuous idempotent is a dcpo, and continuous idempotents are closed under directed suprema.

items.title: Scott topology on an idempotent image
items.summary: The Scott topology on the image of a continuous idempotent is the subspace topology inherited from the ambient dcpo.

items.title: Preliminary adjunction
items.summary: A preliminary adjunction is represented by least elements of inverse upper sets.

items.title: Equivalent adjunction formulations
items.summary: The least-preimage, greatest-preimage, unit/counit, and hom-set inequality formulations of adjunctions are packaged as equivalent data.

items.title: Official adjunction
items.summary: An adjunction between posets is defined by the equivalence x <= u y iff l x <= y.

items.title: Basic laws of adjunctions
items.summary: Adjunctions satisfy composition laws, image order isomorphism, injective/surjective characterizations, and preservation of existing suprema/infima.

items.title: Adjoint criterion for complete lattices
items.summary: A monotone map out of a complete lattice has a lower adjoint exactly when it preserves all infima, and dually for upper adjoints and suprema.

items.title: Adjunctions between dcpos
items.summary: Lower adjoints are Scott-continuous; continuous upper adjoints imply preservation of way-below; for continuous domains the converse is packaged.

items.title: Embedding-projection pairs
items.summary: A continuous embedding-projection pair consists of continuous maps with p o e = id and e o p <= id.

items.title: Embeddings reflect approximation
items.summary: For an embedding-projection pair, e x is way-below e y exactly when x is way-below y.

items.title: Kernel operators and images
items.summary: Kernel operators form a dcpo, determine maximal image elements below a point, preserve existing image suprema, reflect way-below on the image, and are ordered by image inclusion.

items.title: Algebraic images of closure operators
items.summary: For monotone idempotents above the identity on algebraic domains, algebraicity of the image is tied to closure under directed suprema, with the hard converse isolated by an explicit bridge.
items.reviewNote: The raw canonical biconditional no longer stores directed-supremum closure in its left-hand side. The backward construction is proved; the textbook omits the forward proof, which is isolated as a book-omission admit.

items.title: Cartesian product of dcpos
items.summary: The product carrier and pointwise order used for cartesian products of dcpos.

items.title: Products preserve dcpo structure
items.summary: Cartesian products compute suprema and infima componentwise and are dcpos when both factors are dcpos.

items.title: Product projections and mediating maps
items.summary: Product pairing and product maps are Scott-continuous in the local interface.

items.title: Product approximation and bases
items.summary: Way-below, bases, continuity, and compact elements of cartesian products are characterized componentwise, with a reverse continuity result under chosen points.

items.title: Finite products in full subcategories
items.summary: Compares a genuine finite-product object, equipped with terminal and binary-product universal properties, with the cartesian product via the cited external categorical theorem.
items.reviewNote: The source statement is represented by a genuine terminal/binary-product universal-property interface. The PDF cites Smyth [Smy83a] and Jung [Jun89]; Jung [Jun89], Lemma 1.21(ii), was located and states the general cartesian-product comparison. The local theorem remains an explicit axiom bridge and is P2, not P3.

items.title: Separate continuity criterion
items.summary: A function out of a product is Scott-continuous exactly when it is Scott-continuous in each variable.

items.title: Exponential objects as function spaces
items.summary: Compares an exponential object carrying the finite-product hom-order universal property with the Scott-continuous function space via the cited external categorical theorem.
items.reviewNote: The source statement is represented using finite-product and exponential hom-order universal properties. Jung [Jun89], Lemma 1.21(iii), was located and gives the corresponding function-space comparison. The local theorem remains an explicit axiom bridge and is P2, not P3.

items.title: Coalesced sums are pointed dcpos
items.summary: The coalesced sum of pointed dcpos is again a pointed dcpo.

items.title: Coalesced sums as strict coproducts
items.summary: Coalesced sums serve as coproducts in strict pointed categories, with continuous and algebraic closure clauses in the local interface.

items.title: DCPO is complete
items.summary: Arbitrary diagram limits in DCPO are constructed as commuting tuples with coordinatewise directed suprema and projection cones.

items.title: DCPO is cocomplete
items.summary: Arbitrary colimits in DCPO are recorded as an external theorem from the cited literature and left as explicit proof debt.
items.reviewNote: The PDF explicitly cites Markowsky [Mar77], Meseguer [Mes77], Herrlich--Strecker [HS73] via Lehmann--Smyth [LS81], and Fiech [Fie92]. Markowsky's published abstract explicitly states completeness and cocompleteness of the category of chain-complete posets and chain-continuous maps. The adaptation to this project's arbitrary-diagram DCPO interface remains an explicit axiom bridge and is P2, not P3.

items.title: DCPO is cartesian closed, complete, and cocomplete
items.summary: The formal package combines cartesian closure with the complete and cocomplete DCPO statements.
items.reviewNote: Cartesian closure and completeness are constructed in Lean. Cocompleteness is inherited from the explicit external boundary theorem_3_3_2_dcpo_cocomplete, so the aggregate theorem is not P3.

items.title: Strict pointed DCPO is monoidal closed, complete, and cocomplete
items.summary: The strict pointed category is packaged with strict function-space/internal-hom data, the smash tensor-hom order isomorphism, completeness, and explicit cocompleteness proof debt.
items.reviewNote: The strict function-space, smash tensor-hom comparison, and arbitrary-limit construction are formalized. The PDF states strict pointed cocompleteness without proof in the surrounding text, so only that component remains an explicit book-omission admit.

items.title: Pointed DCPO is cartesian closed
items.summary: The pointed category has cartesian closure in the local preorder-based interface.

items.title: Expanding sequences
items.summary: An expanding sequence is a natural-number diagram with identity and composition laws.

items.title: Bilimits of expanding sequences
items.summary: The bilimit carrier, projections, embeddings, limit cone, and colimit cocone are constructed for expanding sequences.

items.title: Criterion for colimiting cocones
items.summary: A cocone over an expanding sequence is colimiting exactly when it admits compatible projection legs and an e-p-pair decomposition.

items.title: Bilimit as a subdomain of any cocone carrier
items.summary: For a colimiting cocone, the bilimit embeds as a subdomain of the cocone carrier through the canonical supremum map.

items.title: Bilimits are colimits and limits in restricted categories
items.summary: The bilimit of an expanding sequence is also the colimit and limit in the corresponding embedding/projection categories.

items.title: Bilimits preserve continuity and algebraicity
items.summary: Bilimits of expanding sequences preserve continuous, omega-continuous, algebraic, and omega-algebraic structure, with basis and compact-union clauses.
